quests.title: Those We Have Kept

dialogue.t: Citlali sure drank a lot last night, huh... Wonder if she's even awake...
Good morning.
Waah! C—Columbina! You, uh, sure know how to make an entrance... What are you doing here?
We just finished filming a last-minute scene, so I came up to get some fresh air.
The others are still down below discussing what the final scene should be.
You mean, how it should end?
Yes. They're torn between whether the heroine should reunite with her old friend or not.
Ah... Because the whole point is that she came to her friend's homeland to search for her, right? Paimon almost forgot the plot...
Yes. Director Furina and Miss Chiori think a tragic ending where the two never meet would be more poignant.
But Director Xavier thinks having the two reunite would make for a more touching and heartwarming ending.
Me? I... I'm not sure...
On a personal level, of course I want to see her again... of course I want to experience that moment where we reunite... even if it's just for the Kameras.
But that means... an actor would have to take her place, and that makes me feel...

dialogue.sit: Don't stress about that for now.

dialogue.t: Huh?
Yeah! Don't look so worried! Making a film is supposed to be fun!
B—Besides, it's all gonna work out! You can trust Paimon on that!
Work out... how?
Uh, well... Y'know...

dialogue.sit: It'll all get tied up in a nice little bow. You'll see.

dialogue.t: Yep! Exactly!
Hehe... Okay. I trust you.
I'll just focus on having fun for now.
Well, well, look who we have here! {NICKNAME} and Paimon!
Aw, the lighting specialist and clapper loader that never were...
Uh, yeah... We kinda went AWOL didn't we. Sorry about that.
Hehe, seriously, don't worry about it. Everything's going smoothly on our end, so just do what you need to do.

dialogue.sit: We'll definitely make it up to you...

dialogue.t: You seem to be in better spirits now, Miss Columbina. I apologize if our earlier discussion put you on the spot...
It's okay, I'm fine now. {NICKNAME} and Paimon talked me through it.
So, what are your thoughts on the ending then? Should we have them reunite or not?
We should... tie everything up in bows.
...Huh?
Citlali, we're here!
Oh, right on time.
Well, yeah... We weren't the ones who drank our weight in alcohol yesterday.
Heh, what? Are you suggesting granny can't handle her liquor? It takes a lot more than that to get me drunk.
Really? 'Cause, uh, you stopped making sense after a while...
Uh... Did I? Huh, news to me. I didn't say anything... too crazy, I hope.
Let's see... You spent half an hour badmouthing Ororon, half an hour complaining about work, an hour talking about light novels... and, uh, Paimon kinda fell asleep after that.
...Are they gone?
Hm? Oh, the crew? Yeah, we bumped into them on the deck, but they just left.
Wait but, now that everything with your core is sorted out, what's stopping you from seeing Columbina? She misses you a lot!
I... I just want to deal with this mess first. Besides, this is the perfect chance to make her jump for once. I have to plan it out more.
But, enough about that. Were you able to pinpoint the location of our target?
Of course. When Granny Itztli promises something, she delivers!
Great, let's see...
The Morte Region... Wait, this is the Tower of Gestalt.
The place the souls were severed... Is that the source of the resentment? Or is it the Narzissenkreuz Ordo in general?
Let me come with. This thing's movement isn't fixed. If it's not at this location when we get there, I can use a ritual to summon it.
You've already gone to more than enough trouble...
I don't mind. These old bones have nothing better to do anyway. Summoning a spirit isn't going to do me in.
(Besides, if I don't go, they'll just have more inside jokes I can't join in on!)
Alright then. I appreciate it.
Hah, there's no time to lose. Let's head out!
Huh, no sign of it so far...
Should I start the summoning ritual?
Let's drain the water from this floor of the tower first. It'll make it easier to move around.
Wait, we can do that?
Of course. Alain and Rene both saw the future that awaited Fontaine, and even shared a few methods for waterproofing buildings. The principle behind it is...
...Ahem, not important. Just unlock the mechanisms in the order I tell you.
Ready?
Yeah. When this thing appears, I'll try talking to the souls inside.
But, more than likely, they've already been driven to madness. If communication fails, we'll have a battle on our hands.
In that case, Paimon better find a hiding spot.
If a fight does break out, I should be the one to deliver the final blow. Trust me on that.
Understood.
Alright, I need quiet.
...Wandering spirits drifting along the tides, hear me now. Broken souls, silenced, torn apart, and forsaken, follow the traces of the past and return to us.
...Let resentment recognize resentment. Let vile entities be drawn together, and in this place, take form once more!
(...What now? Is that it?)
(Ugh... This is exactly why I deal in math not magic. How are we supposed to know what stage the spell is at? It's like there's no logic to speak of.)
(Mechanical science is so much easier to—)
Watch out!
Hey, you! Or whoever's inside of you... I need you to listen to me.
I'm a descendant of Fontaine's "Lord-Artificer," Alain Guillotin. I can make you whole again and return you to the Ley Lines. You just need to work with me here...
Sandrone!
Tch... Looks like talking this out is off the table.
Alright, plan B... Time to blow off some steam!
...Is it over?
Yep. Told you it'd be a piece of cake.
How did you do that back there?
That creature was nothing special. Add a bunch of souls with nowhere to go, a touch of malicious energy, a few impurities, and a whole lot of resentment, and that's what you get.
All I did was separate the original souls from the rest of the filth, allowing them to be accepted by the current rules of the world.
The principle behind the world-formula is "divergence." Starting from a point of origin, it deconstructs and reconstructs the possibilities of the world to find certain answers.
So, it would follow that reverse-calculating the world-formula allows us to achieve convergence and restoration instead. Using the numerological array, I was able to do just that.
It's similar to the concept of homological reduction in mathematics. I reduced them to the basic, fundamental essence of their being, without changing their underlying nature.
That meant... Ugh, never mind. Judging by all the blank stares, I'm guessing you don't actually care.
I think I finally understand how outlanders feel when I ramble on about Shaman stuff...
P—Point is, it was super impressive! You really are amazing, Sandrone!
Hah, you're just realizing that now?

dialogue.sit: I'd expect nothing less from the Unraveller of All Reason...

dialogue.t: Ahem, enough about that!
W—We should get going! I'll go reset the mechanisms inside the tower. See you back on land!
Well, that's one old mess for the books. Glad to have that over and done with.
Feels nice to do a good deed every once in a while.
You helped everyone out a bunch in Nod-Krai, too! Kinda seems like you're just a good person at heart!
Heh, I wouldn't be so sure. I'll be heading back to the Fatui soon enough. You two are too trusting sometimes...

dialogue.sit: Well, at the very least, we know we can trust you.

dialogue.t: Hmph, fine. Just don't say I didn't warn you when it comes back to bite you.
Well, where to next? Back to the ship?
Yeah! Your personal business, the Narzissenkreuz thing, it's all resolved. That means you can "see the people that need seeing" now, right Sandrone?
Everyone's gonna be so happy you're back!
Heh... You wouldn't catch me dead admitting to this before, but... Yeah. I really have missed everyone.
Columbina's a special case, though! This time, I'm definitely getting her back for all her annoying antics over the years!
Um, Sandrone...
Don't ruin the moment. Or I'll start thinking about how you teleported me to a random location after I explicitly told you to stop doing that...
U—Um...
Aaand... Scene! Bravo! Bravo! We got it! This is exactly the ending I was hoping for!
Where did you just go, Miss Columbina? You vanished, and then the next second you were back, hugging this, um... new friend here.
Th—That... was all... on... Kamera...?
Yeah. Well, the Kamera was already rolling, and it happened so fast, so... Yeah.
Hold on, this must be...
Yep, my best friend. The one I was looking for. I never thought I'd actually get to see her again. I'm just... so happy.
Plus, the film got a happy ending too. It's all thanks to you, Sandrone.
...Sandrone?
You couldn't stop being annoying for one second!? Columbinaaaa!

quests.description: Now that she has been “born anew,” what will she choose to do next…?
